title: The foremost
hookLine: the foremost in faith will be foremost that Day, the ones brought near (56:10–11)
tomorrow: The water you drink, the fire you light

cards: A school sports day, the first race about to start. A row of kids, toes on the line, and one already leaning forward before the whistle. Whatever happens at the finish, that's the one who wanted to go.
Surah Al-Waqi'ah has just named the people on the right and the people on the left. Then it names a third group, and says their name twice, like a starter calling it over the crowd.

teach.b: Verses ten and eleven. Pickthall: "And the foremost in the race, the foremost in the race: Those are they who will be brought nigh." In Arabic: was-sabiquna s-sabiqun, ula'ika l-muqarrabun.
Commentators read the doubling two ways. The foremost here are the foremost there: first to good in this life, first on that Day. Or simply: the foremost, and what foremost they are.

Who are they? Early commentators gave many answers, and they fit together: the first to believe in every prophet's time; the first to the prayer when the call is made; the first to repent; the first to do good.
Their reward is a word, muqarrabun, the ones brought near. Near to God.

teach.h: MANY OF OLD, FEW OF LATER TIMES.
teach.b: The next verses add a surprise: a multitude of those of old, and a few of those of later times. Commentators differ on who those are. The Qur'an asks for this eagerness elsewhere too.
Surah Al-Baqarah says: vie with one another in good works. Not compete to beat someone; compete to reach the good first. And the hadith brings it down to the smallest thing.
Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ spoke of two people who'd fallen out and stopped speaking; the better of the two, he said, is the one who greets first.
So being foremost can be as small as saying salam before the other person does.

how: Muslims are encouraged to begin the greeting of salam and to hurry to the prayer and to good deeds; the foremost of these verses are often described as those who are first to good.

o: those first to good, brought near to God
the earliest prophets, sent before all others
the winners of a race on the Last Day

s: the word 'foremost' is said twice in verse ten
was-sabiquna s-sabiqun: the foremost, the foremost.
being foremost means beating other people
Al-Baqarah says vie with one another in good works: compete to reach the good.
the hadith says the better of two estranged people waits to be greeted
the better one is the one who greets first.

games.q: two people have fallen out and stopped speaking. according to the hadith, which one is better?
o: the one who stays silent longest.
games.why: the Prophet said the better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting.

practice: Picture the first few people you'll see after this, someone at home, a coworker, the person at the counter, and imagine catching one's eye and saying hello first, warmly; if you're Muslim, that may be as-salamu alaykum.
If there's someone you've been avoiding, picture them too, and the first word you might say.

wordCard.voice: The foremost. As-sabiqun, those first to good in this life, said twice, and called the ones brought near. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: and the foremost, the foremost. From s-b-q, to go ahead, to win a race.

carryVoice: Your line: first in good. The week ran from Ar-Rahman's balance, refrain, two seas and his face to Al-Waqi'ah's three groups and its foremost. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: And the foremost in the race, the foremost in the race: Those are they who will be brought nigh.
